title: The invariant ring of inertia is etale at the contracted prime
statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite group acting by ring automorphisms on a commutative ring $R$, and let $\mathfrak q\subset R$ be a prime ideal. Write $R^H=\{r\in R:hr=r\text{ for every }h\in H\}$ for the invariant subring of a subgroup $H\subseteq\Gamma$. Put
$$I=\{g\in\Gamma:g\mathfrak q=\mathfrak q,\ g|_{\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak q)}=1\},\qquad\mathfrak q_I=\mathfrak q\cap R^I.$$
Then the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(R^I)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R^\Gamma)$ induced by inclusion is etale on an open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak q_I$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-weil-etale-morphism]. No Noetherian assumption, finiteness of $R$ over $R^\Gamma$, or invertibility of $|\Gamma|$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $A=R^\Gamma$, $C=R^I$, and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$. By [lem-dl-a1-finite-invariant-prime-orbits-residues], $A\to R$ is integral, its fibre is a finite orbit, and its residue extensions are normal with finite automorphism groups. Thus [lem-dl-a1-integral-normal-residue-etale-splitting] gives an etale $A$-algebra $B$, a prime $\mathfrak p\prime$ above $\mathfrak p$, a lift $\mathfrak Q$ of $\mathfrak q$, and a product $S=B\otimes_A R$ with one fibre prime per factor and purely inseparable residues.

source.place: Tag 0BST, lemma-inertia-invariants-etale, first two reduction paragraphs, together with Tag 0BSS, lemma-inertia-base-change.

proof.text: Apply [lem-dl-a1-etale-base-change-inertia-square]: inertia at $\mathfrak Q$ is $I$, $S^\Gamma=B$, $S^I=B\otimes_A C$, and $\operatorname{Spec}S^I\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is etale and maps $\mathfrak Q\cap S^I$ to $\mathfrak q_I$. These identifications persist under principal localization of $B$ away from $\mathfrak p\prime$.

source.place: Tag 0BST, lemma-inertia-invariants-etale, first two reduction paragraphs, together with Tag 0BSS, lemma-inertia-base-change.

proof.text: Integrality of $B=S^\Gamma\to S$ follows again from [lem-dl-a1-finite-invariant-prime-orbits-residues]. Apply [lem-dl-a1-equivariant-fibre-product-refinement] and replace $B,S$ by $B_b,S_b$, with $b\notin\mathfrak p\prime$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] this $B$ is still etale over $A$. The refined factors are permuted by $\Gamma$ and retain their unique fibre primes and purely inseparable residue fields. Relabel the factor containing $\mathfrak Q$ by $1$.

source.place: Tag 0BST, lemma-inertia-invariants-etale, third reduction paragraph: equivariant refinement of clopen pieces and principal localization removing the empty-fibre pieces.

proof.text: By [lem-dl-a1-transitive-product-inertia-component], $\operatorname{Spec}S^I$ has an open component $W$ containing $\mathfrak Q\cap S^I$ with $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}B$ over $B$. Its map to $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is etale by step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map] its image $V$ is open and contains $\mathfrak q_I$. Cancellation with the open inclusion $V\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}C$ makes $W\to V$ surjective etale. The composite $W\to V\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale because it is $W\simeq\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Apply [lem-trf-etale-descent-through-source-cover] to conclude that $V\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale.

source.place: Tag 0BST, lemma-inertia-invariants-etale, final paragraph: decomposition and inertia stabilizers, transitive product invariants, and the first open component.
